meme_jup.notes: Fake-money paper strategy on Solana meme coins using public Jupiter prices; no wallet and no real orders. Each run the scanner reads Jupiter's trending, most-traded and top organic-score lists and keeps coins up at least 10% in 24h, not falling over the last hour, with at least $250k of 24h volume (stablecoins, stock-tracking coins and large-cap majors excluded). A rug check then requires Jupiter verification, an organic score of at least 70, at least $100k liquidity, a trading pair at least 24 hours old, mint and freeze authority renounced, top holders at or below 35%, any dev wallet at or below 10%, a 24h rise no larger than 300% and at least 1,000 holders. Coins that pass get a $500 paper position (maximum 10 open, at most 3 new per run). Fills use the Jupiter USD price plus a modelled 1% slippage and fee on entry and minus 1% on exit. A position is closed at +50% (take profit), -25% (stop), after 72 hours, or if it later fails the rug check (for example liquidity collapsing below $100k). Open positions are marked to the Jupiter price at the latest run; market value is shown before and after the modelled 1% exit cost, and unrealised P&L and equity use the after-cost value. Times are UK time.

jup_earn.notes: Fake-money paper test of Jupiter's November 2026 products: no wallet, no real deposits and no orders. $10,000 split 60% into two stablecoin lending vaults (Bitwise JupLend Optimizer and Bitwise sUSDai Yield, $3,000 each), 30% into the Crypto 6 basket and 10% into a leveraged looping vault (Bitwise sUSDai Multiply). A separate $10,000 control sits in plain Jupiter Lend Earn USDC and is not part of the book's equity. Vaults are marked to the share price shown on the public vault pages; the basket is marked to Jupiter prices of its six coins; both are shown after modelled exit costs where they apply. Modelled costs are assumptions: 0.10% entry cost on vaults and 0.10% price impact on the basket each way, plus the published 0.25% basket fee on exit. Target APYs are curator targets, not measured returns. A vault is exited if its share price falls 2% or more in a day, USDC trades under $0.99, or the vault is delisted; curator pauses and incident reports are checked by hand. Times are UK time.
